---
title: "Install, customize, and update"
---

## Install an exact candidate

Use an immutable candidate revision, not an editable symlink and not an
unversioned moving branch. Before the first candidate commit is frozen,
`CANDIDATE_COMMIT` is a deliberately replaceable placeholder.

```bash
quarto add arfiligol/quarto-design-kit@CANDIDATE_COMMIT
```

Then select the format in a consumer `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
format:
  qdk-html:
    toc: true
    code-copy: true
```

The installed copy belongs under the consumer's tracked `_extensions` folder.
QDK does not fetch fonts, icons, or styles from a CDN.

## Override tokens in the consumer

Create a consumer-owned Sass file, for example `styles.scss`, and list it after
the format theme. This preserves one Kit token authority while making the
consumer's explicit final override visible:

```yaml
format:
  qdk-html:
    theme:
      light: [default, _extensions/qdk/qdk.scss, styles.scss]
      dark: [default, _extensions/qdk/qdk.scss, _extensions/qdk/qdk-dark.scss, styles.scss]
```

```scss
/* Consumer-owned final override: change only a declared QDK token. */
/*-- scss:rules --*/
:root { --qdk-link: #2D5E85; }
```

Render the consumer and inspect the resulting CSS to verify its final token
value. Do not edit a copy inside `_extensions/qdk`; reinstall the exact revision
instead.

## Update

Choose a new exact candidate revision only after reviewing its provenance and
rendering the consumer. Replace the installed extension through `quarto add`
with that exact revision, commit the resulting `_extensions` change in the
consumer, and repeat its own validation. Future release tags are not promised
by this `0.1.0-dev` candidate.
